title: Factorized slow task × fast state coefficients over Vector-Network atoms
hypothesis: A separable task × input-state coefficient view over a shared rank-1 atom bank reconstructs held-out task-state combinations with lower complete bytes than an independent coefficient tensor while preserving per-input local atom inference.
physical_object: K=8 rank-1 weight atoms shared by four tasks and four input states
mirror_coordinate: task factors T[t,r] × state factors S[s,r] × shared atom coefficients H[r,k], rank r=2
local_inference: per input, recompute atom scores |v_k^T x| and choose top-2; state code comes from the known input-state label

fresh.release_rule: Do not open fresh after native CP/tensor factorization alias or frozen gate miss.

controls: native CP/tensor factorization of the coefficient tensor
metrics: active atoms and unique local subsets
pass_gate: Heldout nRMSE <=0.02, at least 25% fewer bytes than independent task-state coefficients, exactly two input-local active atoms with varying subsets, and strict native-control frontier gain.
fail_gate: FAIL Mirror-specific value on native factorization alias, storage gate miss, quality miss, or no strict native-control gain.

compute.active_MACs: K input projections plus top-2 rank-1 outputs
compute.coefficient_decode_MACs: task-state pair times rank-2 basis evaluation, reported separately

boundaries: Synthetic compositional coefficient tensors only; no trained Vector Network or fast-weight learner claim.
Task and state codes are supplied and charged; no task/state inference claim.
The input-local atom selection is executed per example, but coefficient factors are oracle generated from a rank-2 separable teacher.
Native tensor factorization is the direct attribution control.
